project.name: risk_analytics_agent
project.objective: Build a small-scale financial-document intelligence demo, inspired by Moody's multi-agent RAG architecture, as a personal proof-of-work project to show a credit-ratings/DCM finance professional at Adani Group. Scope: (1) ingest a handful of PUBLIC financial documents only - public annual reports, bond prospectuses, disclosures - never confidential or internal company data; (2) classify each page as text-heavy, table-heavy, or chart/image, and route to a matching extraction method; (3) chunk, embed, and store extracted content in a local vector store (Chroma or FAISS, no cloud infra); (4) implement an agentic retrieval loop - plan, search, reflect, iterate, synthesize with citations - instead of single-shot vector search; (5) implement 2-3 narrow specialist agents (credit analysis, ESG/climate, compliance) plus a router agent that decides which specialist(s) to invoke per query; (6) output a structured analysis note with citations, in the style of a first-pass credit-rating rationale note. Runs locally, small scale, built primarily via Claude Code, using the Anthropic API.

assumptions.text: The two corpus documents are annual reports of two different Adani listed entities, not two documents from one issuer. Peer and sector comparison is only meaningful across issuers; if the human supplies two documents from a single entity, the peer specialist must be dropped or the corpus widened.

Four specialists are registered (credit, ESG-climate, compliance-disclosure, peer-sector) but the router invokes at most two per query. This reconciles the stated objective of two to three narrow specialists with the four selected, and is what keeps a single run under the cost ceiling.
Implementation language is Python 3.11 or newer using the official anthropic SDK, on Windows with local file storage. Not yet confirmed by the human.
Confirmed, no longer assumed: the host runs Python 3.11.15, satisfying the Python 3.11 or newer constraint. Verified by python --version on 2026-09-15.

Correction. The bare python on PATH is a Hermes agent venv (3.11.15) with no pip and must not be used. The usable base interpreter is CPython 3.12.5 at AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python312, reached as py -3.12, which satisfies the Python 3.11 or newer constraint. The project venv is created from it, and gate commands continue to invoke .venv/Scripts/python.exe so the shadowed interpreter can never be picked up.

invariants.text: Only publicly published documents are ever ingested, indexed or quoted. No confidential, internal or non-public company data enters the corpus, the vector store or any prompt.

Every material factual claim in a generated analysis note carries a citation resolving to a specific source document and page number that a reader can open and verify. An uncited material claim is a defect.

decisions.title: Embeddings come from a local sentence-transformers model
decisions.text: The Anthropic API exposes no embeddings endpoint, so Claude covers router, specialist and synthesis calls only. Embeddings are produced locally by a sentence-transformers model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 class). Keeps the no-cloud-infra constraint intact and avoids a second API key. Voyage AI voyage-finance-2 was rejected for this demo on cost and second-key grounds; it remains the upgrade path if retrieval quality proves insufficient.

decisions.title: Corpus is public Adani-entity filings only
decisions.text: Ingest only documents published on investor-relations or exchange sites of Adani listed entities: annual reports and public bond offer documents. Each source URL is verified as public before ingestion and recorded alongside the document. No confidential, internal, draft or non-public material is ingested under any circumstance.

decisions.title: Delivery is a CLI that writes a cited Markdown note
decisions.text: A single command takes an analyst question and writes a structured Markdown analysis note to disk in the style of a first-pass credit-rating rationale. No web UI in this release. Streamlit is an explicit non-goal, revisitable after the agent architecture is proven.

decisions.title: Page routing is heuristic first, vision only for chart-suspect pages
decisions.text: PyMuPDF layout statistics (text density, ruling-line count, image area fraction) classify each page as text-heavy, table-heavy or chart-image. Only pages the heuristic flags as chart-image are sent to Claude vision for interpretation. Keeps ingestion cost bounded and the routing decision inspectable and testable without API calls.

decisions.title: The project owner is the sole named independent reviewer
decisions.text: Milap Vaghasia reviews and approves every Genesis gate requiring human sign-off. No other reviewer exists for this project. No approval may be recorded unless he gave it explicitly in session.

decisions.title: Gate commands invoke the project venv interpreter explicitly
decisions.text: Dependencies install into a project-local .venv and every executable gate invokes .venv/Scripts/python.exe directly rather than a bare python. Gate commands must not depend on shell activation state, on which shell Genesis spawns, or on packages present in the user global interpreter. A gate that passes only inside an activated shell is not proof.

decisions.title: Vector store is Chroma, with FAISS as the fallback
decisions.text: Chroma is chosen over FAISS because it persists vectors and per-chunk metadata together, which FR-5 chunk provenance and AC-2 fresh-process queryability both need. FAISS would require a hand-rolled metadata sidecar and its own persistence handling for no gain at this corpus size. The tradeoff accepted is a heavier Windows dependency tree. Installation friction is not assumed away: the T-1 gate imports and round-trips the store, so a failed Chroma install fails that task and triggers the documented switch to faiss-cpu plus a metadata sidecar.

decisions.title: Starting model split is Haiku 4.5 for high-frequency calls, Opus 5 for analysis
decisions.text: Router, reflection verdicts and chart-page vision run on claude-haiku-4-5 because they are high-frequency, short-output and structurally simple. Specialist analysis and final synthesis run on claude-opus-5 because they carry the reasoning quality the demo is judged on. Published rates are 1 and 5 dollars per million tokens for Haiku 4.5 against 5 and 25 for Opus 5, so this split is the lever that makes the NFR-1 ceiling reachable. This is a starting point, not a measured result: AC-8 measures actual per-run spend in T-8 and the split is retuned there if it misses. Both identifiers live at the single configuration point required by NFR-8.
decisions.source: planning 2026-09-15, bundled claude-api skill model table

decisions.title: sentence-transformers is declared but installed at T-4, not T-1
decisions.text: The embedding dependency is declared in pyproject as the optional embed extra rather than a default dependency, and is installed when T-4 first exercises embedding. It pulls torch, roughly two gigabytes, and nothing in T-1 through T-3 touches it. The T-1 store round-trip test supplies explicit vectors, so it proves Chroma persistence without any embedding model present. The cost of this is that a fresh clone running pip install -e .[dev] cannot embed until the extra is installed; T-4 owns closing that.

decisions.title: AC-1 is measured on a holdout split labelled after thresholds were fixed
decisions.text: tests/labelled_pages.json holds 40 human-assigned page labels in two splits. The tune split of 20 was used while setting thresholds; the holdout split of 20 was rendered, read and labelled afterwards and never tuned against. Accuracy is 20 of 20 on holdout and 19 of 20 on tune, against an AC-1 floor of 85 percent. Both are asserted by the T2 gate, so a regression fails the build. Reporting the tune number alone would have been a fitted figure, not a measurement.

decisions.title: Corpus documents stay in sample_pdf and are never committed
decisions.text: The two PDFs live in sample_pdf where the human saved them. config.DOCUMENTS_DIR points there and corpus/manifest.json remains the committed record of what the corpus contains and where each document came from. Both are gitignored: they are public documents, but redistributing them through this repository is not this project's business, and the manifest makes the corpus reproducible from the recorded URLs without them.

decisions.title: Three golden questions, drafted against what the corpus actually contains
decisions.text: Q1 credit, table-only: As at 30 June 2026 what are APSEZ Net Gearing and DSCR, what covenant thresholds do they run against, and how much headroom remains? Answerable only from the covenant calculation table and the Regulation 52 ratio table. Q2 compliance and disclosure: What does the AGEL FY25 auditor report flag as Emphasis of Matter and Key Audit Matters, and what related-party and contingent-liability exposures accompany them? Mixes prose and note tables across both auditor report and notes. Q3 peer and credit, spans both issuers: Compare the disclosed financing profiles of AGEL and APSEZ on debt maturity structure, interest-rate exposure and reliance on related-party or promoter funding, and say which shows more refinancing risk on the disclosed evidence. The three are chosen to force three different specialist selections, which is what AC-7 measures. No ESG-led question is included because the corpus cannot support one.

decisions.title: The retrieval loop has a fourth stop condition: no_progress
decisions.text: FR-9 names three terminations: sufficiency, iteration ceiling, spend ceiling. Implementation added a fourth. When reflection returns insufficient but proposes no query that was not already tried, continuing would spend money to retrieve exactly the chunks already held. The run stops and records no_progress. This is a superset of FR-9 rather than a departure from it, and it is visible in the trace, but the specification does not mention it and should be amended if the human wants the text to match the code.

decisions.title: Citation integrity is enforced in code, not requested in a prompt
decisions.text: Two rules the model cannot override. The router may name any specialists it likes; route() truncates to MAX_SPECIALISTS_PER_QUERY and records which were dropped and why, so FR-13 holds even when the instruction is ignored. Specialists are told to cite chunk ids; consult() then intersects every claim's cited ids against the retrieved set, keeps only real ones, and drops any claim left citing nothing, recording it in dropped_claims. A claim citing an id that was never retrieved is the fabrication case that would most damage credibility with a ratings audience, so it is removed rather than printed with a caveat.

decisions.title: The note surfaces specialist disagreement instead of resolving it
decisions.text: FR-14 requires contradictions to be surfaced. find_contradictions flags pairs of claims from different specialists that share at least three substantive words and disagree in polarity, and render prints both under a Specialist disagreement heading marked as reported rather than resolved. The heuristic is crude and deliberately biased toward false positives: a surfaced non-contradiction costs the reader a moment, while a buried contradiction is a synthesis quietly picking a winner and presenting it with the authority of a single answer.

decisions.title: The sources table marks which documents a note actually cited
decisions.text: The rendered note lists the whole registered corpus under Sources, because a reader needs to know what was available. Listing both documents without saying which were used implied AGEL had been analysed in a note that cited only APSEZ. A used-here column now marks each document cited or not cited, and a test asserts both values appear. Found by reading a rendered note rather than by a failing test.

decisions.title: Model split retuned against measured spend: specialists on Sonnet 5
decisions.text: DECISION-39162611 set Haiku for routing and Opus for analysis as a starting point and said AC-8 would retune it. Measured: one specialist call on Opus 5 cost 0.1393 dollars with evidence already capped, so two specialists plus synthesis could not fit under the 0.25 ceiling; the second specialist and the synthesis were both refused and the note came out incomplete. Specialists moved to Sonnet 5 at 2 and 10 dollars per million against 5 and 25. Synthesis stays on Opus 5 because the note's final prose is what a reader judges. Measured result across the three golden questions: 0.1109, 0.1247 and 0.1904 dollars, all inside the ceiling.

knowledge.title: Anthropic API has no embeddings endpoint
knowledge.text: The Anthropic API provides no embeddings endpoint. Verified against the bundled claude-api skill: its Current Models table and reading guide document no embeddings surface, and the only embedding string match in the skill is unrelated prose in prompt-caching.md. Any embedding step must therefore use a local model or a third-party provider such as Voyage AI.

knowledge.title: Genesis gate commands run through cmd.exe on Windows and must quote the interpreter path
knowledge.text: Genesis spawns gate commands with shell true, which on win32 means cmd.exe. A bare relative path using forward slashes, such as .venv/Scripts/python.exe, makes cmd parse .venv as the command name and /Scripts/python.exe as switches, failing with 'is not recognized as an internal or external command' and exit 1, even though the identical string works in Git Bash. Verified by replicating the exact spawn options. Three forms work under cmd: backslashes, a leading dot-backslash, and the path in double quotes. The quoted form is used because it is the only one that is also correct under a POSIX shell. Any future gate that invokes an interpreter by relative path must quote it.

knowledge.title: Neither corpus document contains any chart page; AC-9 is unreachable as things stand
knowledge.text: Classified all 401 pages. AGEL FY24-25 financial-reports: 204 text, 163 table, 0 chart, and no raster imagery on any page. APSEZ Q1 FY27: 15 text, 19 table, 0 chart, largest figure-sized image 3.9 percent of a page. Confirmed against 40 pages rendered and read by eye across two splits; not one is a chart. Consequences: AC-9 requires a golden question answerable only from a chart page and cannot be satisfied by this corpus, and the FR-3 vision extraction path in T3 will never execute on real data. A tripwire test fails if a chart page ever appears.

knowledge.title: Two layout facts that broke the first classifier, measured on the real corpus
knowledge.text: First: APSEZ Q1 FY27 carries a page-sized raster behind real text on every page, so raw image area is 1.0 document-wide and carries no information; two ordinary pages were classified chart because of it. Images covering 90 percent or more of a page are now excluded from the figure signal. Second: AGEL financial statements rule their rows but not their columns, so requiring both horizontal and vertical rules read the Statement of Profit and Loss and most notes as prose. Horizontal ruling plus modest numeric density is now sufficient. Both were found only by rendering pages and looking at them, not from the feature numbers.

knowledge.title: The ESG/climate specialist has almost no material in the current corpus
knowledge.text: Term counts across both documents: AGEL has emission 1, climate 0, sustainab 2, carbon 4. The 176 hits for ESG are the ESG Overview page-header navigation repeated on nearly every page, not content. APSEZ has none. The supplied AGEL file is the financial-reports extract; the emissions, capacity and transition disclosures live in the Integrated Annual Report sections that were not supplied. Consequence: the ESG specialist can be built and routed but will correctly report insufficient evidence on this corpus. Adding the full AGEL Integrated Annual Report would close this gap and the chart gap in KNOWLEDGE-35fe2525 at the same time, since the ESG sections are where its charts are.

knowledge.title: PDF table cells carry their own line breaks; rendering must collapse them
knowledge.text: APSEZ Q1 FY27 page 34 has a wrapped label that is one cell in the PDF but two physical lines. Rendering rows verbatim produced 19 lines for 18 rows, which silently broke the one-row-per-line invariant that FR-5 no-split-mid-row depends on. Table.to_text now collapses whitespace inside each cell while leaving Table.rows unmodified, so fidelity is kept for inspection and the invariant holds for chunking. Found by a test asserting line count equals row count, not by reading output.

knowledge.title: Gate commands default to a 120 second timeout; slow suites need --timeout
knowledge.text: genesis gate uses 120000 ms unless --timeout is passed. The T5A index suite takes about 206 seconds because it loads the sentence-transformers model, ingests the 34-page APSEZ filing three times across the incremental-reuse tests, and spawns a second interpreter for the fresh-process persistence check. The first attempt failed with a timeout failure, not a test failure. Later gates that touch embedding or the live API need the same flag; genesis gate . <task> --timeout 900000 is what passed.

knowledge.title: Embedding model now loads from cache; the gate fits the default timeout again
knowledge.text: sentence-transformers contacted the model hub on every load to check for updates. Behind a TLS-inspecting proxy that check failed with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, retried five times with backoff, then fell back to the cache anyway, costing roughly thirty seconds per load. Loading with local_files_only first, falling back to a normal load only when the model is not cached, cut load to 10.2 seconds. The full suite went from 224 to 61 seconds and the T5A gate now passes at the 120000 ms default, so --timeout is no longer needed. The earlier record recommending --timeout 900000 is superseded.

knowledge.title: core.autocrlf was true and would have invalidated every Genesis proof
knowledge.text: The repository inherited core.autocrlf=true from global git config. Committed blobs are stored LF but a checkout would rewrite every working-tree file to CRLF, changing content hashes and invalidating the source-bound proof of all completed tasks. This is the same failure that broke T2 completion when a Python write_text call produced CRLF. Set core.autocrlf=false locally after the first commit and normalised the one file, manifest.py, that already carried CRLF. Local git config is not part of the tracked tree, so it does not affect task scope. A clone on another machine will inherit the global setting again and should set it before running any gate.

knowledge.title: Windows writes .env with a BOM, which hid the key entirely
knowledge.text: PowerShell Set-Content -Encoding utf8 and Notepad both prepend a UTF-8 byte-order mark. Read as plain utf-8 the first line parses as a key name carrying an invisible prefix, so it never matches ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and api_key raises key-is-not-set over a file that looks perfectly correct in any editor. Confirmed on this project's own .env, which the human created with the Set-Content command and which does carry a BOM. Fixed by reading utf-8-sig. Tests cover BOM, CRLF, quoted values, surrounding spaces and comments, because every one of those is what a Windows user will actually produce by hand.

knowledge.title: Credential tests must isolate ENV_FILE or a real .env silently disables them
knowledge.text: Three tests in test_config asserted that a missing credential raises. Once a real .env existed on the machine, api_key fell through to it and those tests stopped testing anything, failing with DID NOT RAISE. The .env fallback introduced a dependency on developer machine state that the tests did not account for. An autouse fixture now points config.ENV_FILE at a non-existent path for every test in the module, and fixtures that need a file set it explicitly. Any future credential source added to the resolution chain must be isolated the same way.

knowledge.title: The .env key never reached the SDK: auth resolved in config but not in the client
knowledge.text: First live call ever attempted failed with TypeError, could not resolve authentication method. llm.client() called config.api_key() to validate a key is present, then constructed anthropic.Anthropic() with no arguments, and the SDK resolves credentials from os.environ only. A key living in .env therefore satisfied our own check and was invisible to the client. Confirmed by injecting anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=config.api_key()), which got past authentication to a billing error. The fix is one line in llm.client(), but src/risk_analytics is not in T9A's declared scope, so it cannot be made under the active task. Every test passed throughout because every test injects a fake client and never exercises the real construction path.

knowledge.title: The API key is valid but the Console balance is zero
knowledge.text: With the key injected correctly the API returned 400 invalid_request_error: credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. The key itself authenticates. T9A cannot measure AC-8 per-run spend or run the three golden questions until credits are purchased in the Console. No tokens were billed by the failed calls.

knowledge.title: Structured-output schemas reject maxItems; array bounds must be enforced in code
knowledge.text: The first live structured-output call returned 400 invalid_request_error: output_config.format.schema: For array type, property maxItems is not supported. PLAN_SCHEMA, REFLECT_SCHEMA and ROUTE_SCHEMA all declare maxItems. Whether minItems is accepted is not yet established. This is a second shape defect the whole offline suite could not catch, because every test injects a fake client that never validates a schema against the service. Array bounds have to move into code, which is where FR-13's specialist cap already lives for the same reason: the model is asked, the limit is enforced.

knowledge.title: Four retrieval-quality defects only live runs could expose
knowledge.text: One: reflection rendered the first twelve chunks in insertion order while the evidence set grew, so it never saw new evidence and could not converge, burning every iteration. Fixed by ranking on distance. Two: all accumulated evidence went to every specialist, 52 chunks and 22k input tokens on Opus, twice, which is what breached the ceiling. Capped to the ten best. Three: issuer scoping was defeated by the word and, a token unique to Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, so any question containing and matched both documents and scoped to neither; minimum token length raised to four. Four: the corpus is lopsided at 1666 chunks against 133, so a cross-issuer comparison retrieved 74 chunks all from the larger document and both specialists correctly reported that no comparison could be made. Fixed by retrieving per document and merging. Every one of these passed 192 offline tests.

knowledge.title: The contradiction detector was noise at its original threshold
knowledge.text: On a real run it flagged 11 pairs from 16 claims, nearly all of them two specialists agreeing in different words about different measures. Raised the shared-word threshold from three to eight, deduplicated pairs and capped the section at three. The section is also relabelled Possible specialist disagreement and states that it is a lexical heuristic and not verified, because presenting heuristic guesses as confirmed contradictions in front of a ratings professional is its own credibility failure.

knowledge.title: Balanced retrieval is undone unless the evidence trim is balanced too
knowledge.text: Fixing per-document retrieval was not sufficient for cross-issuer questions. A comparison run retrieved 40 chunks from one issuer and 28 from the other, then rank() trimmed to the ten best by distance and discarded all 28: both specialists saw one issuer only and correctly reported that no comparison could be made. The larger document simply ranks better on average, so any flat top-N reproduces the imbalance the retrieval fix removed. rank_balanced allocates the cap per document and spends any unused share on the next best hits. After the fix the same question cited both issuers, 4 of 11 findings resting on APSEZ, and concluded across both. Two fixes were needed because the imbalance appears at two stages; fixing only the visible one looked like progress and changed nothing a reader would see.

notes: Classifier and offline tests complete: 17 tests, no network, no API key, no model. FR-2, FR-4, NFR-5 and AC-12 are met by the current evidence; AC-1 is not.

AC-1 met on real evidence: 100 percent on a 20-page unseen holdout, 95 percent on the 20-page tuning split, floor 85 percent. The single tuning miss is AGEL p95, a ruled list of entity names with almost no digits.
limitations: AC-1 is not demonstrated. It requires at least 85 percent correct classification over a 20-page stratified sample of the real corpus, and the corpus is still empty. The executable gate passes against seven synthetic pages built with PyMuPDF, which prove the classifier reads the layout signals it claims to read and that its rule ordering is right, but say nothing about whether the thresholds hold on real annual-report pages.
Thresholds in classify.py are first guesses set against synthetic pages. Tuning them against real documents is expected and is what AC-1 measures.
The chart class is unexercised by real data; neither corpus document has a chart page. The chart rules are proven only against synthetic fixtures.

Known failure mode: a ruled table of names with a very low digit ratio, such as AGEL p95, reads as prose. Fixing it by lowering the digit threshold would pull in ruled prose pages; it needs a row-regularity signal, which is not built.

Text pages are extracted as prose and table pages with their row and column structure preserved, each page recording the method actually used; chart pages are recorded and skipped without any model call

scenarios.scope: one real page of each class drawn from the registered corpus
scenarios.environment: local, no network and no API key present
scenarios.observable: each page is extracted by the method its class dictates and records which method ran, table rows survive intact rather than collapsing into a line of prose, and any chart page is recorded as skipped with no model call attempted

notes: Extraction routes by class: prose for text, PyMuPDF find_tables for table pages, chart pages recorded and skipped with no model call. A table page whose grid cannot be resolved falls back to prose and records that it did, rather than emitting unaligned figures that read like a table.
limitations: The chart branch is exercised only against a synthetic page, since the corpus has no chart page. Consistent with the amended FR-3, which withdraws figure interpretation.

Table detection quality is not measured the way page classification was. AC-9 covers it indirectly at T9A by requiring the APSEZ covenant question to be answered from table pages alone; there is no per-table accuracy figure.

tasks.outcome: Extracted content is chunked without splitting a table mid-row, embedded by a local sentence-transformers model, and persisted to a local Chroma store a fresh process can query, with unchanged documents skipped on re-ingest

scenarios.scope: the full 401-page corpus index
scenarios.environment: local filesystem, embedding model running offline, two sequential runs in separate processes
scenarios.duration: one ingest run followed by a second over unchanged input
scenarios.observable: the second process queries the persisted store without re-ingesting and re-embeds no unchanged document, and every retrieved chunk carries document id, page number and page class

notes: Chunking, local embedding and Chroma persistence complete. 21 tests in the index suite, 114 across the project. Table chunks split only on row boundaries with the header repeated; documents fingerprinted by file bytes so an unchanged corpus re-embeds nothing; store proven queryable from a separate interpreter. Covenant figures 0.55 and 5.42 are retrievable from table-filtered search, which is the retrieval half of golden question 1.

Loader fix: model loads from local cache first, so the offline path is the default rather than a fallback after five failed hub retries. Full corpus indexed at 1799 chunks; retrieval sanity-checked against all three golden questions and returns correct pages with checkable citations.
limitations: The embedding model is downloaded once on first use, so the very first ingest on a clean machine does touch the network. Embedding itself does not: a test sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE and still embeds.

Retrieval quality is not measured. The covenant-figure test proves those two values are reachable for one query; there is no recall or precision figure over a question set. AC-5 and AC-9 exercise this indirectly at T9A.
The index suite takes about 206 seconds, so its gate needs --timeout 900000 rather than the 120 second default (KNOWLEDGE for the reason).
First use on a machine with no cached model still downloads it once, about 90 MB. Embedding itself never reaches the network, proven by a test that forces HF_HUB_OFFLINE and TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE.

tasks.outcome: A query is answered by an agentic loop that plans sub-queries, searches, reflects on whether the evidence suffices, revises and retries when it does not, halts on sufficiency or an iteration or spend ceiling, and emits a machine-readable trace of the whole run

scenarios.scope: one query whose evidence is deliberately absent from the first sub-query results
scenarios.environment: local, against recorded model responses so the test spends nothing
scenarios.observable: the trace records more than one iteration, a revised sub-query following an insufficient reflection verdict, and which of the three termination conditions ended the run

notes: Agentic loop complete: plan into sub-queries, search each, reflect on sufficiency, iterate with revised queries, halt on sufficiency, iteration ceiling, spend ceiling or no-progress. 17 tests, all against a scripted model over a real index, so the suite spends nothing and stays deterministic. Trace is JSON round-trippable and carries per-call cost by purpose.
limitations: No call has ever been made against the live Anthropic API. The client wrapper is written to the documented Messages API shape including structured outputs, but no key exists yet, so request shape, structured-output behaviour and token accounting are unverified against the real service. T9A is the first task that proves any of it.

A fourth termination condition, no_progress, was added beyond the three FR-9 names: reflection reporting insufficient while offering no new queries. Looping there would re-retrieve identical chunks at real cost. It is recorded in the trace like the others but is not in the specification text.

tasks.outcome: A router selects at most two of the four specialists per query and records a stated reason for every selection and non-selection, and each specialist answers only from retrieved corpus evidence, reporting insufficient evidence rather than filling a gap from general knowledge

scenarios.scope: the three golden questions of DECISION-70a5ab26
scenarios.environment: local, against recorded model responses
scenarios.observable: the three questions do not all produce the same specialist set, no run selects more than two specialists, every specialist carries a recorded selection or non-selection reason, and the ESG specialist asked about this corpus returns insufficient evidence rather than a manufactured finding

notes: Router plus four narrow specialists. 17 tests; the ones that matter check misbehaviour: over-selection is truncated, unknown specialist names ignored, claims citing non-existent evidence dropped and recorded, a finding with no surviving claims marked insufficient rather than reading as a successful analysis.
limitations: AC-7 is proven with a scripted router, so it shows the machinery routes differently when the model decides differently. Whether the real model actually varies its selection across the three golden questions is measured at T9A.
Specialist prompt quality is unmeasured. There is no eval of whether findings are useful or well-grounded, only that unsupported claims cannot survive into the output.

tasks.outcome: One CLI command turns an analyst question into a Markdown rationale note on disk carrying a structural citation on every material claim, surfacing rather than hiding specialist disagreement, stating the not-a-rating disclaimer, and reporting specialists invoked, iterations and run cost

scenarios.scope: one golden question against the ingested corpus
scenarios.environment: local, against recorded model responses
scenarios.observable: a Markdown note is written whose every material claim carries a document and page citation traceable to a retrieved chunk, which contains the disclaimer and the cost, specialist and iteration report, and in which two conflicting specialist findings both appear rather than one being silently dropped

notes: Synthesis, Markdown note and CLI complete. 20 tests in the note suite, 169 across the project. Citations are assembled from stored chunk metadata; the model names evidence ids and never writes a page number. A synthesised finding citing an id that was not retrieved is dropped and counted in the run record. python -m risk_analytics ingest and ask are separate commands.

Two defects found and fixed after the gate first passed, both surfaced by the human creating a real .env rather than by a failing test: the BOM parsing bug, and test isolation against a real credential file. 179 tests pass.
limitations: The contradiction detector is lexical, not semantic. It will miss disagreements phrased without a polarity word and will flag unrelated claims that happen to share vocabulary. It is a prompt for the reader, not a guarantee.
Note quality has no eval. The tests prove structure, citation integrity and honest degradation; whether the prose is useful to a credit analyst is judged by the human at T9A.
Still no call has been made against the live Anthropic API. Request shape, structured-output behaviour and token accounting remain unverified.
